incidents.vector: Chained zero-day campaign — a BeyondTrust Remote Support flaw for initial access, then an unauthenticated VMware vCenter authentication-bypass zero-day (CVE-2026-123890) exploited with a custom Go-based tool dubbed Bonesaw — to seize administrator control of victims' virtualization stacks.
incidents.impact: The attacker gained full administrative control of vCenter and ESXi environments, stole SAML signing keys to forge authentication tokens, and bypassed MFA. CISA added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog; Broadcom has released patches but lists no workaround.

incidents.victim: 40+ Irish credit unions (via supplier Wellington IT)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in Belfast-based software supplier Wellington IT's mobile banking app platform in early October; the flaw was closed Oct. 6 but the breach went undetected for roughly six weeks.
incidents.impact: Payment details (payee information) for members using credit union mobile banking apps were accessed; over 40 Irish credit unions filed breach notifications, with the incident potentially also affecting U.K. members. No evidence yet of fraudulent transactions or stolen funds.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack claimed by the extortion group "n0n," which listed the retailer on its dark-web leak site; the group has been observed using AI coding agents to write and debug its attack scripts.
incidents.impact: Online ordering and in-store transaction systems were disrupted over the prior weekend, forcing roughly 100 U.S. stores onto alternative transaction procedures. Systems were restored by Nov. 20; no evidence yet that customer financial data was stolen.

incidents.vector: Chinese-speaking operators used the autonomous AI penetration-testing framework Cairn to discover and exploit an unpatched path-traversal zero-day (CVE-2026-133968) in an open-source medical imaging AI application, gaining shell access to university networks.
incidents.impact: Two East Asian universities were breached; one attempt involved 148 autonomous AI actions over 16 hours. Amazon Threat Intelligence discovered the attacker's exposed Cairn server, had the underlying flaw fixed, and worked with a government partner to notify the affected institutions.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack beginning Nov. 19 impacted IT systems and the legislature's website; the intrusion method and whether ransomware was involved have not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: The Legislature's website and certain IT systems were taken offline as a precaution while outside cybersecurity specialists investigate. No other West Virginia state agencies were affected.

incidents.vector: An FBI sting found that ransomware-recovery firm RansomwareHelp, which publicly claimed it never paid ransoms, was secretly negotiating with and paying ransomware gangs for decryption keys while charging victims a large markup.
incidents.impact: The firm's CTO and co-founder, Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar, was indicted for wire fraud; in one case the firm quoted the FBI's fake victim $16,010 after itself paying attackers roughly $6,000. The case follows similar recent DOJ prosecutions of other ransomware-negotiation firms.

incidents.vector: A ransomware cartel listed NVIDIA on its dark-web leak site, claiming to hold stolen data; NVIDIA has not confirmed any breach.
incidents.impact: If substantiated, the claim would be a significant ransomware/extortion attempt against a major chipmaker; as of reporting, no data samples or technical evidence have been independently verified.

incidents.vector: Attackers used the open-source autonomous AI hacking platform ARTEX — the same tool the FBI recently warned is widely used by both criminals and state-sponsored groups — to compromise the Commission's internal personnel systems.
incidents.impact: The Sysper personnel platform, covering payroll, leave requests, medical reimbursements and translation services, was disrupted for more than 10 days starting Oct. 22. The Commission found no evidence of a broad staff data breach or ransom demand; it is the Commission's third disclosed cyber incident this year.

incidents.vector: Threat actors impersonated Mr. Cooper employees in phone calls to the company's IT help desk to fraudulently obtain temporary passwords, bypassing multi-factor authentication to access systems; the underlying breach was first disclosed in November 2023.
incidents.impact: Large amounts of private customer information were stolen. NYDFS fined Rocket Mortgage (which acquired Mr. Cooper) $6.75 million total for MFA failures, a nearly four-year lapse in risk assessments, and seven instances of untimely incident reporting under the state's cybersecurity regulation.

incidents.victim: Americans and Europeans targeted by Southeast Asian scam compounds
incidents.vector: Scam-compound operators and an armed group in Cambodia and Burma ran virtual-currency investment fraud ("pig-butchering") operations, with the armed group providing security and facilitation.
incidents.impact: OFAC sanctioned scam-compound operator Zhao Hui, two armed-group commanders, and two affiliated companies, blocking their US-linked assets as part of the administration's broader campaign (E.O. 14390) against overseas cyber-enabled fraud targeting Americans.

incidents.victim: US technology/defense contractor (believed to be Palantir)
incidents.vector: A Russian national who entered the US illegally via Mexico conducted physical and technical surveillance of company employees near their workplace and homes, using surveillance equipment and receiving taskings from Russian intelligence handlers over Telegram.
incidents.impact: The DOJ arrested the individual for illegal surveillance; prosecutors say the targeting was linked to the company's role supplying weapons-related support to Ukraine.

incidents.vector: A newly identified group exploits SS7 and Diameter telecom signaling protocols to plant backdoors on carrier infrastructure, running commands to collect device data, track subscriber locations, and intercept calls and SMS traffic.
incidents.impact: The group has been active since early 2025 and has used telecom-protocol access to conduct carefully targeted surveillance of selected individuals across multiple Asian countries.

incidents.vector: A threat actor used a cloud access key that Barracuda had issued to a third-party AI service provider and forgotten to revoke to access its cloud environment, then deployed the ARTEX AI penetration-testing framework to escalate access.
incidents.impact: The attacker had access to Barracuda's cloud environment for nearly two days earlier in November before being discovered; the company traced the entry point in a post-mortem and is notifying affected parties.

incidents.vector: Hackers accessed a test environment at Rakuten's Securities division to extract customer account data.
incidents.impact: Data on more than 15 million customer accounts was stolen, including sensitive information for 4.4 million of those accounts; Rakuten says passwords, PINs, and other authentication data were not taken.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack affecting IT systems, disclosed one day after a similar attack on Equinor; no confirmed link between the two incidents has been established.
incidents.impact: IT systems were affected but operations and production were not impacted; no data loss has been identified. The back-to-back breaches prompted other Norwegian energy firms to raise their alert posture.

incidents.victim: 18 EU politicians and law enforcement officials
incidents.vector: A pro-Kremlin hacktivist group published personal information of high-profile targets, including government ministers, Europol and Eurojust officials, and journalists who have investigated Russian hacking and influence operations.
incidents.impact: Victims named in the dox included Italy's foreign minister, Europol's Cybercrime Centre head, Germany's federal police president, and multiple journalists, raising personal-safety and harassment concerns for those exposed.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack affecting internal IT systems, including email; the company says the attack does not appear to be specifically targeting Equinor, and operations/production were unaffected.
incidents.impact: Equinor's email and other internal IT systems were disrupted; as of Nov. 19 the company said it still lacked a timetable for resolution, though it maintained no data had been stolen.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached Ethiopian Airlines' ShebaMiles frequent-flyer loyalty programme.
incidents.impact: Customer data associated with the loyalty programme was stolen.

incidents.victim: French supermarket chains and food retailers
incidents.vector: A military cyber unit within the IRGC's Cyber-Electronic Command sabotaged commercial refrigeration systems, following a similar pattern to earlier freezer outages at US military commissaries in August.
incidents.impact: Refrigeration failed at roughly 700 French retail locations, including butchers, food factories, and a slaughterhouse, causing tens of millions of euros in losses. A five-agency French government report formally attributed the October incident to the IRGC unit.

incidents.victim: Optimizely customers (178+ websites, incl. BBC, CNN, Zoom, Equifax, Ledger)
incidents.vector: An attacker exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely's Web Experimentation platform to inject malicious JavaScript into customer accounts, which was then served from Optimizely's own trusted CDN under its legitimate certificate.
incidents.impact: At least 178 organizations' websites served malware to visitors for about 16 hours, including cryptocurrency wallet-address swapping, payment-card skimming, and iOS/iPadOS exploit-kit delivery. Optimizely patched the flaw and remediated affected accounts within a day.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached the cloud platform of IT and cybersecurity provider N-able, accessing its Mail Assure and SpamExperts servers.
incidents.impact: N-able found no evidence that customer details were stolen and is rebuilding the affected services.

incidents.vector: An attacker exploited a data analysis tool to access the AI coding platform's internal network and copy data from its databases.
incidents.impact: Stolen data includes user details and activity records from the platform; CodinGame has notified affected users.

incidents.vector: A brute-force attack over a weekend compromised user accounts on Germany's e-government platform BundID.
incidents.impact: At least 10,000 user accounts were compromised; officials locked the affected accounts and are notifying owners.

incidents.vector: Threat actors stole tokens across 11 different cryptocurrencies in what researchers call the largest cryptocurrency theft in history, dwarfing the $1.46 billion Bybit hack of 2025.
incidents.impact: Roughly $6.3 billion was stolen; blockchain analysis firms linked the attack to North Korea within days, and the FBI attributed it to the North Korean group it tracks as TraderTraitor. Binance helped freeze about $2.8 billion in stablecoins, and the DOJ separately froze $1.2 billion tied to a related North Korean social-engineering scheme, but roughly $3.25 billion in Bitcoin and Ethereum remains unrecovered.

incidents.victim: Semiconductor manufacturers, defense-policy organizations, and civil-society groups (19 orgs)
incidents.vector: Chinese-speaking operators paired the open-source autonomous AI penetration-testing framework Cairn with Chinese AI models to run 25 largely unsupervised intrusion operations, each broken into reconnaissance, exploitation, and lateral-movement phases without human direction of individual steps.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 confirmed unauthorized access or data theft at 10 of 19 targeted organizations, including over 1 million member records and 31,000 CRM contacts stolen from a US teachers' union, credential theft and rogue admin accounts at a semiconductor supplier, and tampering with a live industry standards-ballot document.
